actions.operation: [OP:POLYNOMIAL_LONG_DIVISION] Divide the dividend by x-1 one degree at a time, subtracting each product before continuing.
[OP:READ_QUOTIENT] Collect the quotient from one degree below the dividend through its constant coefficient and separately verify the leftover constant remainder.
[OP:FACTOR_IDENTITY] Start from the finite geometric identity for x^9-1 as (x-1) times all consecutive powers below the dividend's degree.
[OP:ALGEBRA_REARRANGE] Rewrite the given dividend as (x^9-1)+2 and read the quotient from the factored first term.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:polynomial_long_division] Compute the quotient by the standard repeated leading-term division algorithm.
[KERNEL:geometric_factor_identity] Obtain the quotient from a finite geometric-series factorization without long division.

actions.operation: [OP:COMBINATION_PRODUCT] Compute the unordered choices of three from the seven boys and two from the four girls with binomial coefficients.
[OP:INDEPENDENT_CHOICE_PRODUCT] Multiply the two independent selection counts.
[OP:EXHAUST_CASES] Generate every increasing three-index subset of the boys and every increasing two-index subset of the girls.
[OP:ORDERED_ENUMERATION] Form every pair consisting of one generated boy subset and one generated girl subset, then count the resulting groups.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:binomial_product] Use a closed-form product of binomial coefficients.
[KERNEL:finite_subset_enumeration] Exhaust the two finite subset lists and count their Cartesian pairs.

actions.operation: [OP:SIGN_INVARIANT_BOUND] Convert the absolute-value inequality into its equivalent closed real interval.
[OP:INTEGER_PARITY_BOUND] Apply ceiling and floor to the two interval endpoints and count the integers inclusively.
[OP:FINITE_CASE_ENUMERATION] List every integer between conservative integer bounds just outside the two real endpoints.
[OP:VERIFY_RESULT] Substitute each listed integer into the original absolute-value inequality and count exactly the passing cases.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:interval_endpoint_count] Solve symbolically for the interval, then count its integer lattice points.
[KERNEL:literal_integer_enumeration] Test each candidate integer directly in the original inequality.

actions.operation: [OP:PRIME_FACTORIZE] Factor both given integers independently into prime powers.
[OP:INTERSECT_FACTORS] Take the minimum exponent of each common prime and generate the common two-digit divisors from that exponent lattice.
[OP:EUCLIDEAN_ALGORITHM] Compute the greatest common divisor by repeated quotient-remainder steps.
[OP:DIVISOR_ENUMERATION] Test the two-digit positive integers against that gcd and count those dividing it exactly.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:prime_exponent_intersection] Construct the common-divisor set from independent prime factorizations.
[KERNEL:euclidean_gcd_divisor_scan] Obtain the gcd by Euclid, then scan its two-digit divisors.

actions.operation: [OP:COMBINATION_PRODUCT] Choose which four of the seven islands contain treasure and multiply by the corresponding success and failure powers.
[OP:ARITHMETIC] Reduce the resulting exact rational probability.
[OP:DIRECT_INTERVAL_DYNAMIC_PROGRAMMING] Initialize the probability vector for zero searched islands and update the treasure-count states once per island.
[OP:EXTRACT_COMPONENT] After seven updates, extract the state for exactly four treasures and reduce it.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:binomial_probability] Evaluate the closed-form binomial probability.
[KERNEL:bernoulli_count_dp] Propagate the complete finite treasure-count distribution by dynamic programming.

actions.operation: [OP:ARITHMETIC_MEAN] Use symmetry of an odd-length consecutive-integer list to identify its median with its arithmetic mean.
[OP:ARITHMETIC] Divide the given total by the number of terms.
[OP:ARITHMETIC_SEQUENCE_SUM] Let the first term be an integer and write the full consecutive-series sum using the endpoint formula.
[OP:SOLVE_EQUATION] Solve for the first term, then advance to the unique central term.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:median_equals_mean] Read the median directly from the mean of the symmetric list.
[KERNEL:sequence_endpoint_solve] Solve the arithmetic-series equation for its first term and then index the median.

actions.operation: [OP:PRIME_EXPONENT_ACCUMULATION] Prove from the divisor-count product that an integer has exactly three positive divisors exactly when it is the square of a prime.
[OP:ORDERED_ENUMERATION] Generate primes in ascending order through the ordinal requested in the problem and square the final generated prime.
[OP:FINITE_CASE_ENUMERATION] Traverse positive integers in ascending order and generate each integer's factor pairs.
[OP:DIVISOR_GCD_ENUMERATION] Count distinct positive divisors for each traversed integer and stop when the requested ordinal of qualifying integers is reached.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:prime_square_characterization] Use the divisor-count theorem and ordered prime generation.
[KERNEL:literal_divisor_count_scan] Enumerate integers and their divisors directly until the requested ordinal qualifies.

actions.operation: [OP:PRIME_FACTORIZE] Factor the fixed final term into prime powers.
[OP:PRIME_EXPONENT_ACCUMULATION] Use the integer-ratio geometric-progression relation to require the ratio squared to divide the final term, then maximize the allowed ratio.
[OP:FINITE_CASE_ENUMERATION] Enumerate every possible integer ratio greater than one and no larger than the square root of the final term.
[OP:VERIFY_RESULT] For each ratio, test whether dividing the final term by its square gives a positive integer first term, then select the value satisfying the ordering constraints.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:factor_exponent_constraint] Solve the geometric progression through prime exponents.
[KERNEL:integer_ratio_scan] Exhaust the finite range of possible integer ratios and test each one.

actions.operation: [OP:CONSTRUCT_OBJECT] Contract the three named people into one super-person while retaining every internal ordering.
[OP:COMBINATION_PRODUCT] Count circular arrangements of the contracted objects, multiply by the internal permutations, and quotient rotations only once.
[OP:FINITE_CASE_ENUMERATION] Fix one labeled person at a reference seat, generate every permutation of all remaining labeled people, and place them around the table.
[OP:VERIFY_RESULT] Retain exactly those generated circular seatings in which the three named people occupy one consecutive cyclic run, then count them.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:circular_block_contraction] Use the standard super-person block formula.
[KERNEL:fixed_anchor_permutation_scan] Exhaust anchored circular permutations and filter by cyclic adjacency.

actions.operation: [OP:INDEPENDENT_CHOICE_PRODUCT] Condition on the color Alice transfers and determine that color's multiplicity in Bob's enlarged bag.
[OP:DIRECT_RATE_DEFINITION] Identify the necessary and sufficient return-color event and form its favorable-over-total probability.
[OP:ORDERED_ENUMERATION] Enumerate every equally likely first-color choice and, for each, every labeled ball Bob could return.
[OP:FINITE_CASE_ENUMERATION] Mark the ordered outcomes that restore both bags to equal color contents and divide their count by the full outcome count.

strategies.plan: [KERNEL:conditional_multiplicity] Condition on the transferred color and compute the return probability from its multiplicity.
[KERNEL:labeled_transition_enumeration] Exhaust all labeled two-step transitions and count successes.
